transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
I spend so much time checking and trying to fix this one thing about how I look that it’s taking over my day and costing me work. It has just gotten completely out of hand lately.

Are these repeated checking behaviors mainly because you feel there is a flaw in your appearance that other people barely notice, or are they driven by intrusive thoughts or fears that feel hard to control even when they are not specifically about your looks?

It's entirely about how I look—I feel like my face looks incredibly old and worn-out, with these deep lines and gray hair that others say they barely even notice. I end up spending hours in the mirror and taking selfies trying to hide it, so it's definitely driven by my appearance rather than other unrelated thoughts.

Do you think your face truly looks old and worn out despite what others tell you, or is part of you able to recognize that your concern might be exaggerated? How convinced are you that this flaw is real?

To be honest, it feels completely real to me, and I am deeply convinced that my face looks incredibly old and worn-out. Even when people tell me they don't see it, I'm certain it's the first thing everyone notices and judges me for, constantly comparing me to younger or more polished men. I just can't shake the feeling that it's a glaring, undeniable flaw.

Have you ever believed with complete certainty that your face is deformed or abnormal, to the point that no amount of reassurance could possibly be true? Or do you ever have moments when you wonder if your mind might be exaggerating it?

Most of the time, I'm completely convinced it's real, and I feel like my daughter or coworkers are just being polite while secretly judging my appearance. I do have fleeting moments where I wonder if I'm overthinking it, but that doubt quickly vanishes. The conviction that I look incredibly old and worn-out always takes right back over.

Is your worry only about your face looking old and worn out, or are you also very preoccupied with your body weight or becoming fat? Have you been restricting food, bingeing, or purging because of these concerns?

No, my worries are strictly about my face looking old and worn out, specifically the deep lines and the gray at my temples. I don't worry about my body weight or becoming fat at all. I have never had any issues with restricting food, bingeing, or purging.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a persistent preoccupation with a perceived defect in appearance (face looking 'incredibly old and worn-out') that others barely notice, accompanied by repetitive appearance-related behaviors such as mirror checking and taking selfies to hide the flaw. The concern is not focused on weight or fat, ruling against an eating-disorder-type body image concern. The belief is held with very poor insight, approaching delusional intensity, but remains centered on appearance, consistent with body dysmorphic disorder under ICD-10 F45.2.
